subject: HorizonAI - Reserved capacity term safeguards & tiered rebate structure
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas@horizonai.com>, HorizonAI Procurement <procurement@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HorizonAI - Reserved capacity term safeguards & tiered rebate structure

Lucas / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. Following up with a concise framing of what we discussed on reserved capacity sizing and how we can protect HorizonAI (and Redwood) from short-term GPU market shocks while keeping a clean path to committed pricing. High level: HorizonAI is interested in a 12–18 month reserved commit for a mix of A100-equivalent and T4-equivalent slots to support inference at scale; you asked for protections if market GPU spot/lease costs move materially during the term.

Proposal (initial):
- Term: 12 months (preferred) with optional 6-month extension based on usage thresholds.
- Baseline: committed 2.5M token-units/month (mapped to approximate vGPU hours; see attached forecast).
- Cost protection triggers: if the Redwood GPU cost index (monthly average across our sourcing channels) increases by >25% vs. the baseline quarter, HorizonAI is eligible for a tiered rebate/credit applied to the next invoice.
- Rebate structure: 10% credit for 25–40% index increase, 20% credit for 40–60% increase, capped at 25% for >60% increase. Credits apply to consumption charges only, not to base subscription fees.
- Alternative: indexation clause where price per token is adjusted by a capped passthrough formula (we can detail options A/B/C in a spreadsheet).

Attached: HZN-187-draft-MA.pdf (draft master agreement with placeholders for triggers), horizonai-usage-forecast.xlsx (your numbers + ours).

Ask: please confirm whether the rebate tiers above map to HorizonAI's risk tolerance and whether we should instead propose a cap-and-collar with an escrowed credit pool. Once you confirm direction, I’ll loop in Sales Ops and Finance for approval and get Legal to draft the clause.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lucas Reed <lucas@horizonai.com>

Date: 2025-10-16T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: HorizonAI - Reserved capacity term safeguards & tiered rebate structure

Jordan —

Appreciate the follow-up and clear framing. A few quick clarifying Qs from our procurement/finance side:
1) How do you calculate the "Redwood GPU cost index" operationally? Is this an internal blended lease/spot price we can audit?
2) We need the triggers to tie to a public (or auditable) reference if possible — otherwise the escrow option is preferable.
3) Can you map your rebate tiers to concrete $/vGPU-hour deltas for our CFO — we work in committed vGPU-hours, not tokens.

From HorizonAI: our initial committed baseline is targeting ~6,000 vGPU-hours/month (A100 class) in the first 3 months ramping to ~40,000 vGPU-hours/month steady state. I attached our internal forecast; the numbers in your spreadsheet are close but I circled a few line items.

If we can get a simpler fallback (cap-and-collar + escrow), procurement will be more comfortable signing earlier.

Best,
Lucas

Attachment: horizonai_forecast_procurement.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas@horizonai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Options for GPU pricing sensitivity & approval path (HZN-187)

Lucas / Jordan —

I pulled three pragmatic options Sales Ops + Finance can approve quickly. I’m including the rough math; precise $/vGPU-hour mapping is in pricing-options-v2.xlsx attached.

Option A — Fixed unit price + tiered rebate (Jordan's framing):
- Fixed committed price per token (or per vGPU-hour equivalent).
- Rebate tiers paid as credit on subsequent invoice if monthly Redwood GPU index > X against baseline.
- Finance approval threshold: credit <= 15% overall annualized impact without additional exec sign-off.

Option B — Indexation passthrough (monthly adjustment):
- Unit price adjusts monthly by a capped formula: new_price = base_price * (1 + min(max((index_month / index_base)-1, -0.10), +0.30)).
- Requires legal to accept monthly variation; Finance prefers if cap <= +30%.

Option C — Cap & collar with escrow pool (preferred by Procurement):
- Put 2% of monthly invoice into an escrow that funds credits when index spike occurs.
- Escrow draws down based on pre-agreed waterfall; unspent escrow returned at term end.
- This contains retail impact and spreads cost across term.

Approval notes:
- Ben (Sales Ops) can approve Option A up to 15% annualized credit exposure.
- Anything >15% or requiring multi-quarter escrow sizing needs Marissa (VP Sales) sign-off and Finance (cc'ing) confirmation.
- Legal (Karthik) will draft the trigger language and should aim for an auditable feed (we can reference the 3rd-party GPU price index we use internally).

Next steps: Jordan — please confirm which option HorizonAI prefers; if Procurement prefers escrow, we’ll run a short financial sim and present final ask to Marissa for sign-off.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-18T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for GPU pricing sensitivity & approval path (HZN-187)

Team —

I reviewed Ben's options. For a deal of this scale (HZN-187 projected ARR > $1.2M), I will approve the following conditional guardrail without needing exec escalation:

- Approve Option A (Fixed + tiered rebate) with the following limits: credits capped at 15% annualized impact and rebate tiers adjusted to 8% / 16% / 22% for the 25–40% / 40–60% / >60% buckets respectively.
- If procurement requests the escrow (Option C), Finance must size the escrow; anything that increases Redwood's expected cost exposure beyond 20% requires CFO sign-off.
- Require Legal to include a 30-day review window for contested index calculations and reference the agreed 3rd-party index URL.

Jordan — please present these limits to HorizonAI and confirm acceptance. If they insist on a larger protection, escalate to me with a clear net revenue impact simulation.

Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Lucas Reed <lucas@horizonai.com>

Date: 2025-10-20T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: HorizonAI - Reserved capacity term safeguards & tiered rebate structure

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks — HorizonAI reviewed the limits and we can accept Option A with the adjusted rebate tiers (8% / 16% / 22%) provided: (1) the baseline index is established from Redwood's published feed and auditable monthly; (2) the first trigger only applies after the first three months of live traffic (to avoid a short-term procurement blip); and (3) DocuSign flow and SOW are ready within 7 business days so we can hit our Q4 ramp.

We made one small ask on the draft MA: ensure credits are applied to consumption charges and can roll forward for up to 90 days if HorizonAI has a cash timing issue.

If that looks good, send the final MA + SOW DocuSign link and procurement will start signatures.

Lucas
Head of Cloud Ops | HorizonAI
